newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to allow women troops, draft choice for men.
newsitem.headline: Italy to allow women troops, draft choice for men.

text.p: The Italian cabinet approved plans on Wednesday to open Italy's armed forces to women and to allow men drafted for military service to opt for alternative community work.

The plans, which now go to parliament in the form of draft law, could revolutionise Italy's army, navy and air force, which have depended heavily on conscripts but are slowly moving towards an all-professional base.
A cabinet statement said women aged between 18 and 26 would be able once the law took force to apply for a career in the military or volunteer for the proposed community work scheme.
The Defence Ministry would draw up the necessary procedures governing the recruitment and career paths of women within six months, it said.

The centrepiece of the draft law will give young Italian men the opportunity for the first time to avoid conscription by opting for community work in hospitals, social homes and other welfare facilities.
Under the plan, either service will run for 10 months though the statement said community workers would need an additional three months' training.

"The idea stems from the principle of allowing every citizen the option to choose, on the basis of personal convictions, between two different ways of fulfilling institutional obligations with equal dignity and recognition," it said.
The community work programme would also be open on a voluntary basis to resident foreigners.

Italy calls up a set number of conscripts each year. Many young men miss the draft because they are surplus to requirement or obtain exemption on medical or family grounds. They will be able to volunteer for community work, the statement said.
The draft law received a mixed reception, with some critics arguing that it would cut across a pending law on conscientious objection that is already making its way through parliament.
